title: BandzWagon:
headline: BandzWagon turns seats and turf from the old Buffalo stadium into rings. Co-founder Kathleen Thompson tells the story, and Del Reid from 26 Shirts shows his ring to the camera.
story: BandzWagon's description: BandzWagon turns authentic materials reclaimed from the old Buffalo football stadium into meaningful rings you can wear every day. From stadium seats and turf to seat metal, each piece carries a little bit of The Ralph and the memories made there.
Two voices: Kathleen tells why she made it, and Del Reid from 26 Shirts shows a real ring on his hand and reacts to it. The ring photos show what she is talking about.
do: Open on Kathleen with the hook text on frame 1.
Show the BandzWagon logo at 0:04, when she says the name.
Hold shots 2 to 3 seconds; this client likes slow pacing.
Match the Ms Eye Candy cut: ombre open and close, the standard series end card.
Show the ring photos when she names the seats and the turf.
Use his two ring close-ups: they show the seat backs on a real hand.
dont: No logo, wordmark or name at 0:00.
Do not put the BandzWagon logo or name on the end card. The end card is the same for every boutique.
Do not use her Lashbrook part (about 00:57 to 01:10): it shows another company's website.
Do not use her website line at the end (about 01:16 to 01:20).
No double captions: do not put purple caption boxes over her own burned-in captions.
From the 26 Shirts clip, use only the two lines on this page. Not his intro, not the 26 Shirts plug, not the tag-in-the-comments part, not the WGR tailgate line.

transcript:
Machine transcript of the BandzWagon clips (sent 28 Oct). Times are mm:ss in each clip. It hears the name as 'Bandwagon': it is BandzWagon. Caption what you hear.
--- bandzagon intro.mov ---
[00:00] How do you turn a lifetime of Sunday memories into something that you can wear?
[00:04] That's the idea behind BandzWagon. I'm Kathleen Thompson, one of the co-founders,
[00:08] along with my husband Charlie and our partners Todd and Kim Saxton. I'm also
[00:12] the owner of George Thompson Diamond Company, the jewelry business my dad started in 1977.
[00:16] I grew up in the industry. I've seen how much meaning a piece of jewelry can hold.
[00:20] Sometimes it represents a person, sometimes a milestone,
[00:24] and with BandzWagon, it represents a place. Think about everything
[00:28] fans associate with their stadium. Their first game, going with
[00:32] their parents, taking their own kids, and all of those seasons cheering together.
[00:36] We wanted to give people a way to carry that piece of history with them.
[00:40] Our first collection celebrates Buffalo and the stadium so many fans know as the Ralph.
[00:44] We use authentic reclaimed materials, including stadium
[00:48] seating and field turf, and incorporate them into rings. You can actually
[00:52] see those materials in the inlays. Different designs highlight different
[00:56] parts of the stadium, so you can choose the one that means the most to you.
[01:00] Coming from a jewelry family, the quality matters to me just as much as the story.
[01:04] We work with ring manufacturer Lashbrook in Utah to turn
[01:08] these unusual materials into finished pieces of jewelry.
[01:12] The stadium is part of your story, and this is a way to keep a piece of it. Take a look at the
[01:16] collection at [website] and tell us your favorite memory of the Ralph.
--- AQMk….mp4 (26 Shirts clip: use 00:24 to 00:31.5 and about 00:35 to 00:41 only) ---
[00:00] Hey guys, I am so excited to share with you a new partner that 26 Shirts has. It's something you can wear, but it's not clothing. Our new partner, BandzWagon, … is doing all kinds of different rings
[00:20] and different options for those. All made, look at this, from seats from the Ralph. … I actually have a real ring and it's got blue and red seat backs built into the design there.
[00:40] These things are beautiful. … I'm going to tag them in the caption below. And they're also going to be with us at the tailgate this
[01:00] Sunday before the game with WGR. Alright, take care. Let's go Buffalo.
